frontmatter.title: Api Overview

blocks.content: Aspose.3D for Python provides core 3D `scene` management capabilities through classes like `Scene`, `Node`, and `Entity`. It supports loading, manipulating, and saving 3D models with animation and geometry data.

import aspose_3d_foss

# Create a Scene instance
obj = aspose_3d_foss.Scene()

# Access root node
result = obj.root_node()

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Scene` | Represents a 3D `scene` containing nodes, `entities`, and `animations` |
| `Node` | Represents a `transform` node in the `scene` hierarchy |
| `Entity` | Base class for 3D `entities` like meshes and cameras |
| `AnimationClip` | Contains animation data across multiple channels |
| `AnimationChannel` | Represents a single animated `property` over `time` |
| `Geometry` | Defines vertex and index data for mesh geometry |
| `Camera` | Represents a camera `entity` for rendering |
| `FileFormat` | Specifies supported 3D file `formats` |
| `AssetInfo` | Holds metadata about the 3D asset |
| `CustomObject` | Allows custom data attachment to `scene` objects |

Aspose.3D provides a structured Python API for working with 3D scenes, supporting core operations like `scene` graph manipulation, animation, and geometry handling. The `library` follows a hierarchical design where the `Scene` serves as the top-level container, and `entities` such as `Node`, `Entity`, and `AnimationClip` form the `scene` graph with hierarchy support.

Developers can build 3D python game engines, visualization tools, or export pipelines using the public API surface. Classes like `AnimationChannel`, `AnimationNode`, and `BindPoint` enable precise control over keyframe-based `animations`, while `Geometry` and `Entity` support mesh and object definition. File format handling is provided through `FileFormat` and format-specific modules such as `FbxFormat.py`.

| Class | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [`A3DObject`](#) | Base class for all 3D objects with `name` and `properties` |
| [`AnimationChannel`](#) | Represents a single animated `property` with keyframe data |
| [`AnimationClip`](#) | Container for animation data including `start` `time` and `description` |
| [`AnimationNode`](#) | `Scene` graph node that holds animation state and sub-nodes |
| [`BindPoint`](#) | Binds animation channels to `scene` graph elements |
| [`Camera`](#) | Defines camera `properties` for 3D rendering |
| [`Entity`](#) | Base class for `scene` graph elements with parent-child hierarchy |
| [`Extrapolation`](#) | Controls behavior of animation outside keyframe range |
| [`FileFormat`](#) | Abstract base for file format definitions |
| [`Geometry`](#) | Encapsulates mesh data such as vertices and faces |
| [`INamedObject`](#) | Interface for objects with a `name` `property` |
| [`AssetInfo`](#) | Metadata about the 3D asset |
| [`CustomObject`](#) | Placeholder for user-defined 3D objects |
| [`GlobalTransform`](#) | Represents global transformation matrix |
| [`ExtrapolationType`](#) | Enum defining extrapolation modes |

Aspose.3D supports common 3D `scene` construction patterns through its node hierarchy and animation system. The `scene` graph is built around `Entity` objects that support parent/child relationship management, enabling hierarchical organization of 3D objects, lights, and cameras.

Animation is managed via `AnimationClip`, `AnimationNode`, and `AnimationChannel` objects. An `AnimationClip` contains multiple `animations` and can create nested `AnimationNode` hierarchies for complex motion paths. Each `AnimationNode` exposes `bind_points` that link to keyframe sequences via `BindPoint` objects.

| Class | Role |
|-------|------|
| `Entity` | Base class for `scene` graph nodes with parent/child management |
| `AnimationClip` | Container for `animations`, `start` `time`, and `description` |
| `AnimationNode` | Hierarchical animation node with bind points and sub-`animations` |
| `BindPoint` | Links animation channels to `entity` `properties` |
| `AnimationChannel` | Defines animated `property` with keyframe sequence and default `value` |
| `AssetInfo` | Stores file metadata and asset information |
| `Camera` | Represents a camera `entity` in the `scene` |
| `Geometry` | Defines mesh geometry data |
| `FileFormat` | Specifies supported import/export `formats` |
| `Extrapolation` | Controls behavior of animation outside keyframe range |
| `CustomObject` | Placeholder for user-defined 3D objects |
| `GlobalTransform` | Stores world-space transformation matrix |
| `A3DObject` | Base class for named objects with `properties` |
| `INamedObject` | Interface for objects with a `name` `property` |

For 3D python game development and visualization, developers typically construct scenes by attaching `Entity` instances to a root node, then applying `AnimationClip` objects to drive motion. The `parent_node` and `parent_nodes` `properties` on `Entity` enable runtime `scene` graph reorganization.

Developers building 3d python game or 3d python visualization applications can use Aspose.3D to manage `scene` hierarchy and object references. The `library` supports `entity` and `material` attachment for 3d content creation workflows.
